tests: R20 pdfgen's shapes (non-ASCII text in six fonts, every structure, revisions, empty-password RC4 and AES, a heavy page among light ones, a huge page) are read by pdf.js exactly as the truth says, page by page

R20 a PDF under a user password is refused without it and read with it; its truth states ENCRYPTED for every page

R22 a table of any row count and a paragraph of any length are read whole by LibreOffice
R22 the shape ladder: one-cell tables, empty paragraphs, tiny paragraphs, hyperlinks and nested tables hold equal bytes in the main part, and LibreOffice reads every rung's units
R22 templates and macro flavours carry their content types, extensions and macro part; an encrypted member and a package that declares more than it holds are written as named

R22 the encoding matrix: text, JSON, XML and HTML in UTF-8, UTF-8 with BOM, UTF-16 LE and BE, Latin-1, Windows-1252 and with a bad byte decode to the truth's units; each charset declaration is where it is named
R22 deep and unterminated markup: Chromium reads every unit of a 300-deep and of an unterminated page and of a client-rendered shell; unterminated XML is malformed in the truth and to Python's parser

tests: R10 a conforming archive is laid out in APPNOTE 6.3's form: each local header and its data in order, then the central directory, then the end record, with true CRC-32 and sizes, bit 11 exactly for a non-ASCII string name, and one fixed MS-DOS time
R11 a conforming archive with at least one entry passes both oracles: unzip -t exits 0, and Python's zipfile lists the entries in order with their names and gives back each entry's data byte for byte
R12 duplicate names: two entries with one name are written as two entries, nothing merged or renamed
R12 unsafe and non-UTF-8 names: a name is written verbatim, and utf8:false clears bit 11 over non-ASCII raw bytes (a CP437 name)
R12 central directory and local header disagree: local:{…} is what that entry's local header states, field by field and together, and its central record keeps the true values
R12 central:{…}, the reverse: the central record states the override, the local header keeps the true values, and a localOffset past the archive's end writes an entry out of range

R12 bit 3: dataDescriptor sets bit 3, writes zero CRC and sizes in the local header and a data descriptor after the data; descriptor:{…} overrides what it states and signature:false omits its signature

R12 ZIP64: an entry's zip64 writes its sizes and offset as 0xFFFFFFFF with the true values in a 0x0001 extra field; options.zip64 writes the ZIP64 end record and locator with the end record at its sentinels; zip64Record overrides what that record states
R12 encrypted: traditional sets bit 0, strong bits 0 and 6, aes method 99 with a 0x9901 extra field, directory bit 13; the data is written as given, never encrypted
R12 overlap: sameDataAs points an entry's central record at an earlier entry's local header and data, so their byte ranges coincide
R12 the end record: eocd:{…} is what it states, field by field; comment is the archive comment as a string or bytes; secondEocd writes a second well-formed candidate inside the comment
R12 nesting: an entry's data may itself be makeZip's output, read back as an archive inside the archive
R13 deterministic: the same entries and options give the same bytes on every call

R13 no clock, no randomness, nothing written to disk: with the clock and every random source made to throw and the file system made to refuse writes, a child gets the same bytes, and its working and temporary directories stay empty; importing the module has no side effect
R13 a spec it cannot write throws an Error naming the field: an entry without name or data, a sameDataAs naming no earlier entry, an unknown encrypted value

R14 zipBomb writes one deflated kernel of zero bytes once and that many central entries all pointing at it, each declaring the kernel's size, so the declared total is kernel × entries while the archive stays near one kernel's compressed size
R14 nestedZip writes an archive depth levels deep, each level fanout entries each the next level's archive, the deepest fanout copies of leaf, stored or deflated
